page.layout: One page of running text. Running head and page number at the top. Heading "INTENTIO I." with its subtitle, then "ARTICVLVS I." and the body in one column. Catchword at the lower right. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: paratas avolare. Hæc sunt quæ Deo dante extra
dubium ponenda suscepimus; non quidem seorsum
singula probando; sed ex iis quæ natura suggeret,
vel singulis, vel simul junctis, per necessariam con-
sequentiam omnia deducendo. Age igitur Lector,
& hanc partem non ingratam nec inutilem gratus
accipe.
INTENTIO I.
De diversitate partium compositarum, ex
quarum harmonia totum resultat.
ARTICVLVS I.
Superius necessario non pauca præmisimus,
quæ id quod propositum fuimus ostendere non ob-
scure designant; Non tantum prima elementa
in misto seu mavis composito manere, sed diver-
sissimas quibus mistum constat, particulas, ex iis
primis rerum principiis diversimode constructas;
quas secundas, docendi gratia vocare liceat. Ex his
secundis varie coëuntibus, tertiæ fiunt non minus
quàm secundæ inter se differentes. Eundem in mo-
dum, & ex tertiis quartæ, & ex quartis quintæ fieri
intelliguntur. Ad cuius rei confessionem nos vel in-
vitos ducit experientia in rei cuiusvis dissolutione.
Quippe, res in ea resolvitur, ex quibus componi-
tur. Atqui compositum naturale non primo resol-
vitur in prima illa elementa, sed in partes quasdam
inter se natura discrepantes; quarum singulæ spe-
cies rursus in alios multiplices dividuntur; & hæ in
alias minutiores concluduntur. Sæpiusque hæc par-
tium diversarum in minutiores semper diversas sub-
divisio repetitur. Exemplo sit uva, quæ pressa in
mustum

page.notes: The first word of the body is a large initial S joined to "Vperius", read as "Superius". "Vperius" is a vowel, so I wrote U-based spelling per rule 5 only where it fits; the V/U in the initial is set by the woodcut letter and not checked further. Long s is printed as f in many words (fuscepimus, feorsum, fingula, miftum, constructas, diffolutione, refolvitur); all are written with plain s. The catchword "muftum" is read as "mustum". A small red mark at the foot of the page is a stain or stamp and is not transcribed.
